A_target.statement:
Each draw yields one of $n$ coupon types uniformly at random, independently.
Let $T$ be the number of draws needed to collect all types.
Then:
:$\expect T = n H_n = n \displaystyle \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \frac 1 k \sim n \ln n$

B_source.statement:
Let $Y$ have the [[Definition:Geometric Distribution|geometric distribution]] on $\set {1, 2, \ldots}$ with success probability $p$.
Then $\expect Y = \dfrac 1 p$.

substitutions.the single geometric waiting time: the waiting time for each new coupon type

object_map.reformulation: Split the collection into phases, each ending when a new type appears, and sum the geometric means.

validity_conditions: Within a phase the draws are independent trials with constant success probability.
Linearity of expectation handles the sum of the phases.
proof_plan: Write $T = T_1 + \cdots + T_n$, where $T_i$ is the number of draws taken while exactly $i - 1$ types have been seen.
During phase $i$, each draw is new with probability $p_i = \dfrac {n - i + 1} n$, independently, so $T_i$ is geometric with parameter $p_i$.
By the source result, $\expect {T_i} = \dfrac n {n - i + 1}$.

By linearity, $\expect T = \displaystyle \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n \frac n {n - i + 1} = n H_n$, and $H_n \sim \ln n$.
{{qed}}
